reason: Section 1 adds to section 1 of Executive Order 10900 a subsection (d) under which the Secretary of Agriculture, after consultation, "shall transmit" to the Congress "all reports required by Section 408 of the Act". Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-strike-and-insert.md the added subsection continues as part of Executive Order 10900 until that order ends. Executive Order 12220 of June 27, 1980, section 1-501, revokes Executive Order 10900 as amended, and is effective on signing, so the first end is June 27, 1980 (actor: the President by Executive Order 12220; mechanism: express revocation of the amended parent). Executive Order 12220 reissues the reporting direction in its own text, which is a separate command and not a continuation of this clause.

Section 2 amends Executive Order 10900 by revoking "Section 5 thereof and redesignating Sections 6, 7 and 8" as sections 5, 6 and 7. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-strike-and-insert.md the amendment continues as part of Executive Order 10900 until that order ends, which Executive Order 12220, section 1-501, effected on June 27, 1980 by revoking Executive Order 10900 as amended. The alternative reading, that this one-time instruction was exhausted when executed on January 19, 1977, is disclosed for the reviewer; the later date is used for consistency with the amendment ruling and does not change the order-level end because section 1 also ends on June 27, 1980.

The order's operative sentence in the held printing reads that the President exempts Joseph W. Austin from the provisions of section 204 and does "continue him in the service until March 1, 1938", and the recital states the same period ("continued in the service until March 1, 1938"). The President is the actor and the stated date is the end by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive of March 1, 1938 under owner ruling 2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; on the exclusive reading the exemption ends when March 1, 1938 begins. No earlier end is shown by any held source and no later order extends it.
